answer_text:
Let

\[
F(m)=\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\gcd(r,m).
\]

A standard divisor-count argument gives

\[
F(m)=\sum_{d\mid m} d\,\varphi\!\left(\frac{m}{d}\right),
\]

because there are \(\varphi(m/d)\) residues \(r \pmod m\) with \(\gcd(r,m)=d\).

This function is multiplicative. In particular, if \(m\) is squarefree and \(m=\prod p\), then

\[
F(m)=\prod_p (2p-1),
\]

since for a prime \(p\),

\[
1\cdot \varphi(p)+p\cdot \varphi(1)=(p-1)+p=2p-1.
\]

---

### First sum

\[
A=\sum_{n=1}^{1009}\gcd(2n,2020).
\]

Since \(2020=2\cdot 1010\),

\[
\gcd(2n,2020)=2\gcd(n,1010).
\]

Thus

\[
A=2\sum_{n=1}^{1009}\gcd(n,1010).
\]

Now \(1010=2\cdot 5\cdot 101\) is squarefree, so

\[
F(1010)=(2\cdot 2-1)(2\cdot 5-1)(2\cdot 101-1)
=3\cdot 9\cdot 201=5427.
\]

The full sum \(F(1010)\) includes \(n=0\), whose term is \(\gcd(0,1010)=1010\). Therefore

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{1009}\gcd(n,1010)=5427-1010=4417.
\]

So

\[
A=2\cdot 4417=8834.
\]

---

### Second sum

\[
B=\sum_{n=0}^{1008}\gcd(2n+1,2019),
\]

which is the sum of \(\gcd(k,2019)\) over all odd residues \(k \pmod{2019}\).

We have \(2019=3\cdot 673\), with \(673\) prime, so

\[
F(2019)=(2\cdot 3-1)(2\cdot 673-1)=5\cdot 1345=6725.
\]

Now count only odd residues. For a divisor \(d<2019\), residues with \(\gcd(k,2019)=d\) are of the form \(k=dj\), where \(0\le j<2019/d\) and \(\gcd(j,2019/d)=1\). Since \(2019\) and \(d\) are odd, \(k\) is odd exactly when \(j\) is odd.

For any odd modulus \(m'>1\), exactly half of the reduced residues modulo \(m'\) are odd, because \(j\) and \(m'-j\) form pairs of opposite parity. Hence the odd part of the divisor sum is half of the full sum, except for the term \(d=2019\), which corresponds to \(k\equiv 0\pmod{2019}\), an even residue.

Therefore

\[
B=\frac{F(2019)-2019}{2}
=\frac{6725-2019}{2}
=\frac{4706}{2}=2353.
\]

---

Finally,

\[
A-B=8834-2353=6481.
\]

\[
\boxed{6481}
\]
